sections.heading: What is CPL (Cost Per Lead)?
paragraphs: Cost Per Lead (CPL) measures how much money you spend on marketing or advertising to acquire a single lead. A lead is a potential customer who has shown interest in your product or service by providing contact information or taking a qualifying action. CPL is distinct from CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost), which measures the cost to acquire an actual paying customer.

bullets.label: ROI Calculation
bullets.text: Essential input for calculating overall marketing ROI when combined with conversion rates

sections.heading: How to Calculate CPL
paragraphs: Example: If you spend $5,000 on a Google Ads campaign and generate 50 leads:
sections.formula: CPL = Total Marketing Spend / Number of Leads Generated

sections.heading: Organic vs Paid CPL
paragraphs: Organic marketing channels (SEO, content marketing, social media) typically deliver 30-50% lower CPL than paid channels, though they require longer timeframes to generate results.
